title: Measuring E° against the hydrogen electrode
caption: The standard hydrogen electrode, H₂ at 100 kPa bubbling over platinum in 1 mol dm⁻³ H⁺ at 298 K, is defined as 0 V. Connected to Cu²⁺/Cu, the voltmeter reads 0.34 V with copper positive: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V.
alt: Left: hydrogen gas bubbling over a platinum electrode in acid. Right: copper in copper sulfate. A salt bridge and a voltmeter reading 0.34 V join them.
description: Standard hydrogen electrode: Pt, H₂ at 100 kPa, H⁺ at 1 mol dm⁻³: H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻.
Copper half-cell, 1 mol dm⁻³ Cu²⁺: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu.
